title: Your first trade: the credit spread
summary: Sell an option with a bought one behind it: premium in, worst case fixed from day one, and margin that fits a small account.

questions.q: What makes a credit spread a safer first trade than a naked sold option?
options: The bought option caps the loss
questions.why: The bought strike is a floor: the loss can't go past it.

options: Sell a put, buy a put further down
Buy a put, sell a call
Sell a call, buy a call further up
questions.why: The bought put below the sold one caps the loss on a fall.

questions.q: Sell the 500 call at ₹6, buy the 520 call at ₹2, lot 500. What is the credit?
Same trade: what is the worst case?
Why does a spread usually fit a ₹2 lakh account when a naked sale may not?
options: Margin follows the worst case, and the spread's is capped
questions.why: The exchange blocks margin for the worst case; capping it shrinks the margin.
